job_application.reformulated_text: You must regularly report the companies to which you have submitted job applications. These job applications trigger the sending of new potential job offers to you. The companies that received your applications must confirm receipt and rate the applications. You and the company can negotiate a job interview. If a company wants to hire you, you enter a probation phase with that company. After the probation phase, you can rate the company, and the company can rate you. However, the reviews for a company are only visible to job applicants after a period of 1 year has passed. If the job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless you rated the company a C or lower, in which case you will continue to receive job offers, but you will no longer be required to report the companies to which you have applied.

maternity_leave.reformulated_text: A process is created to support planning, taking, and extending a maternity leave. The process starts by fetching information about potential maternity leave models, including their duration in months and how the leave can be split between parents. The parent is then allowed to select a model. After the selection, relevant information is collected from the parent. The collected information is used to notify Social Security and the Company in a timely manner. The process also involves gathering information from companies. At the end of the selected leave period, the parent is given the opportunity to decide whether to extend their maternity leave.

work_accident.reformulated_text:
A process for gathering information about work accidents and almost work accidents involves several steps and applies to different groups of people, including those in insured gainful employment, kindergarten children, schoolchildren, students, and self-employed individuals.

For those in insured gainful employment, a work accident is considered to occur in various circumstances, such as when the accident happens in a location, at a time, and with a cause related to the insured employment, when working from home, on the direct route to or from work, during training sessions, or when visiting a doctor with prior notification to the employer. Accidents that occur while using advocacy groups or professional associations are also considered work accidents.

For kindergarten children, schoolchildren, and students, an accident is considered a work accident if it occurs in a location, at a time, and with a cause related to their education, during school events, on the direct route to or from school, or while performing practical tasks prescribed by the curriculum.

In agricultural or forestry establishments, accidents can be considered work accidents even if they do not occur directly while performing the insured employment, including working in the household of the owner or providing neighbourhood assistance.

Certain accidents outside of professional activity are also considered the same as work accidents, such as activities under unemployment/labour market support services, assisting with an accident, donating blood, or training as a member of a volunteer aid organisation.

Employees must immediately inform their employer of any work accident, near accident, serious and immediate risk to safety and health, or defect discovered in protection systems. The employer must immediately report any work accident resulting in a fatality or serious injury to the Labour Inspectorate if it has not been reported to the emergency services.

Every work accident resulting in a fatality or injury that prevents a person from working for three days must be reported to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days. Self-employed individuals must report accidents involving themselves or their employees to the accident insurance provider in good time.

Students and schoolchildren must report accidents to the competent directorate, and schools, educational facilities, and universities must report every work accident resulting in physical injury or death to the responsible accident insurance provider within five days.

In cases of private insurance, the insured party must report an accident in writing immediately to avoid the provider being released from their obligation to perform, and fatalities must be reported within three days, even if the accident has already been reported.
